mechanism: Denosumab inhibits RANKL and can cause hypocalcemia, which may lead to hyperkalemia through altered potassium regulation and reduced renal potassium excretion secondary to hypocalcemia-induced changes in acid-base balance.
action: Monitor serum potassium and calcium levels regularly; assess for hyperkalemia signs; consider potassium supplementation cautiously and only when clinically indicated with frequent laboratory monitoring.
